name: Qwen3-30B-A3B
notes: The small-active-count MoE case that makes Qwen3 popular for single-node serving. Vendor: 30.5B total / 3.3B activated; safetensors total 30.53B; our config arithmetic gives exactly 30.5B total / 3.3B active. kv_cache_bytes_per_token = 48 layers x 4 kv_heads x head_dim 128 x 2 x 2 bytes = 48 x 4 x 128 x 2 x 2 = 98,304 B/token (96 KiB). GQA, not MLA. MoE: 128 experts, 8 per token, NO shared expert (shared_expert false - Qwen's MoE does not carry DeepSeek's always-on shared expert, so active params are exactly the 8 routed). first_k_dense_replace is absent, i.e. all 48 layers are MoE. hidden 2048 with moe_intermediate_size 768 - a narrow, many-expert design. gqa_ratio 8 (32 heads / 4 kv heads). Context 40960, rope_theta 1000000. Apache-2.0. The serving point: 3.3B active means decode FLOPs are tiny (6.6 GFLOP/token) while 30.5B of weights must still be resident - this is a pure memory-bandwidth problem, and it is why it runs well on one consumer GPU where a dense 32B will not.
